newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - Dutch grocery chains merge to take on Ahold.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dutch grocery chains merge to take on Ahold.

text.p: Regional Dutch supermarkets chain De Boer Winkelbedrijven NV said on Wednesday it planned to merge with unlisted sector rival Unigro NV to create a grocery combine ranked second only to Dutch market leader Ahold.
"The planned merger will be on equal terms...and is expected to make a clearly positive contribution to earnings per share of the new combine...from 1997," the two firms said in a joint statement.
They said the new combine, De Boer Unigro NV, will rank among the top 20 Dutch companies in terms of sales, with annual turnover of more than six billion guilders ($3.5 billion).
With a 13 percent share of the Dutch supermarkets sector, De Boer Unigro will be catapulted into the groceries big league behind market leader Ahold, which controls a hefty 37 percent of the market.
The companies said the merger would be effected through a share swap.
Shares in unlisted Unigro, owned by its former chairman Eric Albada Jelgersma, will go to De Boer Winkelbedrijven in return for shares in the new venture De Boer Unigro.
This would give Unigro's holding company an initial stake in the new combine of 57 percent, to be reduced to 49.9 percent within six months, the companies said.
Part of the new De Boer Unigro shares will be placed with an independent foundation.
Unigro's present owner will, through his holding company, also receive one million warrants on De Boer Unigro shares.
These could be swapped for new shares in the combine at a strike price of 105 guilders a share within five years after the warrants have been placed, the statement said.
However, exercise of the warrants should not result in a further increase of the holding company's economic interest in the combine, it added.

After integration of the two partners, the new combine will operate about 380 supermarkets in the Netherlands. It also owns the Super El Arbol supermarkets chain in Spain and wholesale units in the Netherlands and Belgium.
Unigro posted a net profit of 25.2 million guilders in the 1995/96 financial year on turnover of 4.12 billion.
De Boer is smaller but more profitable with a 1995 net profit of 33.2 million guilders on turnover of 1.68 billion.

Separately, British food and drinks group Grand Metropolitan is unlikely to have a taste for Dutch spirits firm BolsWessanen NV despite takeover speculation that included GrandMet as a potential predator, drinks analysts said.

A GrandMet spokesman would not comment specifically on the rumours, but said the group's new chief executive John McGrath, who took over earlier this year, had said several times the firm aimed to focus on organic growth rather than major acquisitions.
